newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Philippines/Hong Kong air accord looks likely.
newsitem.headline: Philippines/Hong Kong air accord looks likely.

text.p: The Philippines will finally sign a new air services agreement with Hong Kong when talks are held later this month, according to a member of the Filipino delegation.

Benjamin Solis, managing director of Pacific East Asia Cargo Airlines (PEAC) and member of the Philippines panel, told Reuters that the latest round of talks will be held in Hong Kong on September 20 and he is optimistic that an agreement can at last, be reached.

The agreement is the last still to be signed before China takes control of Hong Kong next year but negotiations have already broken down twice this year over air cargo issues, an industry source said.

"The Philippines panel has finally come to an agreement to sign up with Hong Kong during these next talks, without any preconditions, which is the position I have been pushing with the panel during the last few rounds of talks," Solis said.
He said the last round of talks, held in Manila last month, failed because flag carrier, Philippine Airlines demanded fifth freedom rights out of Hong Kong .

"The preconditions were actually Philippine Airlines' position because it wanted more rights out of Hong Kong, especially fifth freedom rights which I think is ridiculous to ask at this time," Solis said.
His five-year-old airline, PEAC, which claims to be the official cargo flag carrier of the Philippines, is in growing competition with Philippine Airlines in the air cargo market, sources said.
Philippine Airlines have so far declined to comment.
Previous agreements have been signed by the British government but because of Hong Kong's handover to China next year, any new deal must be ratified by the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group.
